Are you an expert in ensuring uptime and high quality in a Data Center, or would you like to become one? Then here is a unique opportunity to oversee the operation and maintenance of multiple data centers!

If you have the following, this job is for you:

• Technical education: It can be as a marine engineer, electrician, refrigeration technician, energy technologist, automation technologist or similar

• Relevant experience with Critical Facilities: e.g., Electrical, mechanical, generators, automation, HVAC, buildings automation etc.

• Practical experience with troubleshooting and servicing technical installations

• Experience from operations in a technical environment - preferably data centers

• Meeting customer and government security screening requirements are required for this role

About the role and the team

GlobalConnect operates 11 data centers in Denmark and even more in the other countries where GlobalConnect is present. In addition to the ongoing operation and maintenance of our existing Data centers, there are also large expansions in the pipeline. As our new Data Center Critical Facilities Engineer, you will be part of the Site Operations department with over 45 skilled team members, with colleagues in Norway, Finland, Sweden, Denmark and Germany and with employees from many nationalities, enabling you to work in a multinational environment.

Site Operations Denmark is a workplace with focus on a good working environment. We focus on professional and personal well-being and emphasize good working relationships. Through your work as a Critical Facilities, you will have the chance to engage with every facet of managing a data center. You will experience flexibility in relation to your everyday life and a large degree of freedom under responsibility. You can also expect that most days you will be met with exciting projects and tasks that ensures no workdays are the same.

Moreover, you will have an important role being an essential part of the rotational 24x7 on-call system, also having the requirement to work overtime, reflecting the continuous nature of data center operations as a Data Center never sleeps. Based on these requirements, it would therefore also be beneficial if you are able to reach our Taastrup site within approx. 45 minutes.

Key Responsibilities and what you will do during a typical week:

• Preventive & Corrective Maintenance: Perform rounds and inspections to conduct preventive and corrective maintenance on critical systems. Inspect and test important equipment such as backup generators, cooling systems, UPS batteries, and electrical panels to ensure optimal performance and early detection of faults.

• Physical Monitoring & Inspections: Carry out daily inspections on infrastructure components to assess technical performance, environmental conditions, and compliance with safety and operational standards.

• Incident & Emergency Response: Monitor and respond rapidly to system alerts, alarms, and emergencies.

• Complex Problem Solving: Troubleshoot and assist with repairing of complex issues across electrical, mechanical, and control systems. Apply systematic problem-solving techniques and escalate when needed.

• Change Management: Support the execution and documentation of system changes, following established Change Management protocols to minimize operational risk.

• Vendor Supervision: Coordinate and supervise external vendors to ensure adherence to operational procedures, safety requirements, and quality standards during maintenance or installation work.

Who we are looking for

You are a dedicated professional with a strong commitment to operational excellence and safety in Mission critical environments. With a blend of technical knowledge and hands-on experience, you are skilled at handling complex systems and processes and thrive in roles where critical infrastructure demands unwavering attention. You are detail-oriented, quick to respond to emergencies, and focused on developing and adhering to robust procedures. Your adaptability and communication skills enable you to work effectively with team members, vendors, and contractors alike.

Do you want to play a key role in ensuring the quality and reliability of advanced drone systems used in mission-critical operations? As Quality Control Inspector at Sky-Watch, you will be responsible for inspecting, testing and verifying components to ensure compliance with technical specifications, quality standards and regulatory requirements. You will work hands-on with advanced technology and complex electronic components, contributing directly to the quality, safety and reliability of Sky-Watch’s products.

Working closely with Engineering, Production, Purchasing and Operations, you will identify and address quality issues, support continuous improvements and ensure accurate documentation and traceability throughout the production process. You will become part of a growing Quality function, where you will collaborate with experienced colleagues and have opportunities for professional development and technical specialization.

You will report to the Quality Control Manager and become part of the Operations team**.**

Your key responsibilities include:

• Inspection & Verification – perform incoming inspections of UAV components, assemblies and finished systems against technical drawings, specifications and quality requirements.

• Quality Compliance & Documentation – ensure compliance with internal procedures, applicable standards and customer requirements while maintaining accurate inspection reports, test results and traceability records.

• Non-Conformance Management – identify, document and handle quality deviations through Non-Conformance Reports (NCRs) and support corrective and preventive actions.

• Supplier Quality & Collaboration – collaborate with suppliers and internal stakeholders to address non-conforming materials, resolve quality issues and support continuous improvement**.**

To succeed in this role, you have a couple of years of experience within quality inspection or quality control in a manufacturing environment, preferably from industries such as electronics, telecommunications, satellite technology, aerospace, UAV or other high-reliability manufacturing environments. You bring hands-on experience with mechanical, electrical and/or electronic component inspection, ideally including printed circuit boards (PCBs), small electronic components and precision assemblies. You have a relevant technical educational background, preferably within electronics or a related technical field. Familiarity with IPC standards, ISO 9001 or AS9100 is considered an advantage, as is experience with ERP systems and digital quality management tools.

You are based within reasonable commuting distance of Sky-Watch’s location in Støvring, and are comfortable communicating in both Danish and English.

As a person, you are detail-oriented, systematic and quality-conscious with a strong sense of responsibility and a keen eye for identifying deviations and potential improvements. You combine analytical thinking and technical curiosity with a practical, hands-on approach to problem-solving. You work independently and maintain a structured approach to your tasks, while enjoying close collaboration with colleagues across different technical and operational functions. With a high level of integrity, reliability and commitment to quality, you thrive in a dynamic environment where precision, teamwork and continuous improvement are essential.

Are you the new Quality Control Inspector at Sky-Watch? If so, please submit your application and CV as soon as possible. We encourage all qualified candidates to apply regardless of gender, age, sexual orientation, ethnicity or religion. For further information about the position, please contact consultant Martin Tveit, Sensu A/S, by phone at +45 26 83 38 42.

For more information about Sky‑Watch, please visit www.sky-watch.com.

Please note that applications are reviewed on an ongoing basis, and no application deadline is set.

Would you like to help Whiteaway Group’s engineers spend less time working around tools and infrastructure, and more time building software?

We’re modernizing the platform behind software development at Whiteaway Group. We’re moving away from legacy systems, expanding our cloud platform and automating more of the work that slows teams down. We’re looking for a Platform Engineer to join our Platform Squad in Aarhus and help make it easier for our engineers to build, deploy and run software.

We treat our platform as a product, and our engineers are the people who use it every day. You’ll work directly with development teams to understand where they lose time, decide what to improve and see whether the changes make their work easier.

What you’ll help us achieve

Make it easier for teams to deploy and run their software. You’ll improve CI/CD pipelines and build self-service tools so teams can handle more routine tasks themselves. You’ll work with developers to find the steps that cause delays or require manual work, then help simplify or automate them.

Help us move away from legacy infrastructure while keeping the platform reliable. You’ll build and operate infrastructure on AWS and Kubernetes, using Terraform to make changes repeatable. You’ll also improve monitoring and observability so teams can spot and diagnose problems, and help make secure access easier to manage.

Shape how we improve the developer experience. You’ll help the squad decide which platform improvements will make the biggest difference to development teams. We’re also exploring where AI could help the platform squad and the teams we support, and you’ll have room to test ideas where they solve a real problem.

What you’ll bring

You might be a Platform Engineer, DevOps Engineer, Cloud Engineer or Site Reliability Engineer. You might also be a software engineer who has spent a significant part of your time building or operating cloud infrastructure.

We’re interested in what you’ve improved and how you went about it. Perhaps you’ve automated a deployment that used to require several manual steps, made a production issue easier to diagnose, or built a tool that helped other engineers work more independently.

We’re looking for hands-on experience in several areas of our stack: AWS, Kubernetes and Docker, Terraform, Linux and networking, and Git, GitHub and CI/CD. Experience with Node.js or Go is also relevant. If you’ve worked with GitOps, Argo CD, Datadog, Spacelift, Cloudflare or cloud security, that’s a plus.

Your team and how we work

You’ll join four Platform Engineers in a Tech organisation of around 45 people. Whiteaway Group is one of Scandinavia’s largest e-commerce companies for home appliances, with more than 300 employees. As we continue investing in the platform, you’ll have a say in what the squad builds and how we support development teams across the business.

We make time for learning and sharing knowledge through pair programming, hackathons and Improvement Mondays. You’ll also have access to learning resources and personal development opportunities.

We work primarily from our Aarhus office and offer one fixed day per week to work from home. We also offer a pension scheme, a lunch scheme, an on-site gym and free parking.

Interested?

Send us your application and CV via our careers site. We’d love to hear about a platform, tool or workflow you’ve improved: what problem you tackled, what you changed and what difference it made.

We review applications and hold interviews on a rolling basis, and we’ll hire as soon as we find the right person.

Whiteaway Group is an ambitious, successful and fast-growing e-commerce and retail company. We sell white goods and premium home products to customers throughout the Nordics via several online shops and the Skousen franchise.

The idea for Whiteaway Group arose in the backroom of a Danish kitchen store. The foundation was innovation, business acumen and excellent customer experience. And it still is. Many years later we are the leading supplier in Scandinavia in our field and we are almost 300 dedicated employees working from offices in Sweden, Denmark, and Norway.
